clue.text: Jack adopts necktie, as temperature shifts — it's hot

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the sailor is taken into the middle of the tie
shifts says the temperature letter changes position within the tie, travelling from its end to its front

parts.note: an ascot is a broad neckerchief-style tie
a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)

explanation.surface: A sailor puts on a cravat while the weather changes, and someone remarks on the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor here, not a name or a playing card; the definition is the brief 'it's hot', describing the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: The brand-name pepper sauce is famously fiery, so the clue's closing phrase describes it.

clue.text: Piece of gossip from bird had an impact

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
bit, past of bite, means took effect, had an impact

explanation.surface: A rumour came from a bird that made a big impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A juicy morsel of news, a small tasty item of scandal.

clue.text: Standard member of the censorship board?

definitions.meaning: a standard is a flag carried aloft
a censor is one who bans things, read whimsically

explanation.surface: A typical member of a body that bans films.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag on a pole is a standard; jokingly, a censor is one who prohibits.

clue.text: Polo, say, left aboard ship on campaign around East

indicators.note: aboard puts the left side inside the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship
port is the left side of a ship

indicators.note: the campaign word goes around the east letter

parts.note: a war is a military campaign
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Polo played on board a ship during a military campaign in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polo' is the shirt, not the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A polo shirt is an example of casual athletic clothing.

clue.text: Suppose ID's needed when extremely offensive outside

indicators.note: the extreme letters go outside the identifier
extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number, a form of ID

explanation.surface: Identity documents are thought necessary when things turn nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an opinion or to venture a view, which is what supposing means here.

clue.text: Man on horseback who investigates rogue soldiers

parts.note: a private investigator is a PI
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A mounted officer looks into misbehaving troops.
explanation.definitionFit: In bullfighting the lancer who goads the bull rides a horse, so he is a mounted man.

clue.text: George Michael perhaps enters with Ginger Spice, briefly

parts.note: pops in means drops in, enters

indicators.note: briefly means cut short by a letter

parts.note: Ginger Spice was Geri Halliwell of the Spice Girls

explanation.surface: One 1990s pop star turns up alongside a Spice Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: George Michael was a chart vocalist, an example of a pop artist.

clue.text: Restrict where some cars are parked, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals a sound-alike: the word heard, not the word written

parts.note: cars park by the kerb, the British spelling of the pavement edge

explanation.surface: Limit where certain cars can be parked, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: To curb is to restrain or hold in check.

clue.text: Kitty's cross about check on entry

indicators.note: about means the combined pieces are turned round

parts.note: a kitty is a pot of shared money, and 's here makes it plural
a rood is a cross or crucifix

explanation.surface: A cat is cross about a check at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitty' is a pool of money, not a cat; POTS ROOD reversed reads DOOR then STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge or block that stops a door moving checks it in the entrance.

clue.text: Tea taken with EastEnders? Or else switching over that is

indicators.note: switching over means the letters are switched about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: Tea with soap-opera viewers, or else they change the channel.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a BBC soap set in London's East End; 'Rosie Lee' is Cockney rhyming slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockneys of East London use the rhyming phrase in place of the word for the drink.

clue.text: Depart by bronze steps

parts.note: a bronze colour is a tan
to depart is to go

explanation.surface: Someone leaves past a set of bronze stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine dance is a sequence of steps, steps being a loose term for a dance.

clue.text: Not easily influenced, but not very autocratic

indicators.note: the phrase tells us to take the first word but leave out the very abbreviation

parts.note: someone impervious is unmoved by persuasion

explanation.surface: A description of a ruler who is stubborn without being fully despotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Domineering and overbearing, as an absolute ruler acting without consultation would be.

clue.text: One nearest a certain phase of sleep is at the point of death

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the one next to you is nearest
REM is rapid-eye-movement sleep, the dreaming phase

explanation.surface: Someone closest to a stage of deep sleep is about to die.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means in the most extreme circumstances, especially on the verge of dying.

clue.text: Ancient slave might be partial to pastures new

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An old servant might fancy a fresh start somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial to' reads as 'fond of' but means 'part of'; the definition comes before it, phrased as 'might be'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Anglo-Saxon word for a labourer or slave is a crossword staple for a serf of old.

clue.text: Pepper was associated with such fields in the 60s

definitions.text: Pepper was associated with such fields in the 60s

parts.words: Pepper was associated with such fields in the 60s
parts.note: the Beatles' Sgt Pepper era came with the song about such fields, released in 1967

explanation.surface: A grower's note that a vegetable was once linked to certain crop fields.
explanation.walkthrough: Pepper looks like the vegetable but is Sgt Pepper; 'Strawberry Fields Forever' was recorded in the same sessions in 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: The Beatles song title names fields of this soft fruit, linked to the Sgt Pepper sessions.

clue.text: Dilapidated area illuminated by Australian falling over in wind

indicators.note: in places the lit-and-Australian part inside the word for wind

parts.note: to wind is to twine, coil round
illuminated means lit up, light

indicators.note: falling over turns the Australian abbreviation upside down, which in a down-style reading reverses it

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia

explanation.surface: A rundown area is lit up by an Aussie who keeps toppling in the gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' is the verb to coil, not the breeze; 'falling over' turns the Oz abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for a run-down, ill-defined urban district, besides its sense of an uncanny realm.

clue.text: Allow head of Geography to occupy rocking chair like a sloth

parts.note: to allow is to let

indicators.note: the first letter goes into the jumbled seat letters
a rocking chair moves back and forth, so the word is shaken up
the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A geography teacher is allowed to sit idly in a rocking chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish and lacking energy, as the slow tree-dwelling mammal seems to be.

clue.text: Jack laid down by players in card game — clever! I'm to play

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
East and West are two of the four players in bridge
sharp means clever

explanation.surface: A jack is played at bridge; a clever move, says a player.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the first person: the instrument speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A small instrument plucked between the teeth is something to be played.

clue.text: Devious guards reportedly cheated with rigour

indicators.note: guards means surrounds, so the sly word goes outside

parts.note: devious means sly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for cheated is used for its sound only

parts.note: cheated means tricked

explanation.surface: Crafty security guards are said to have cheated with rigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Done strictly means done rigorously, with no laxity.

clue.text: Dentist perhaps starts to fret about new air-conditioning

parts.note: a dentist pulls teeth, so is one who extracts

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A dentist starts worrying about new cooling in the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventilation device that pulls stale air out of a room is a form of air-conditioning, loosely.

clue.text: Shake bedspread? Not left time before vicar's turning up

indicators.note: not means the left and time letters are removed

parts.note: a quilt is a bedspread

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a vicar is a Rev, reverend, and 's is is, linking

explanation.surface: A vicar shakes out a bedspread before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble slightly, a synonym for shake.

clue.text: Cast includes lead in laughable piece of armour

indicators.note: includes means the threw word contains the first letter

parts.note: shied means threw, cast

indicators.note: the lead in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A theatre cast includes a comic lead in a suit of armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like actors but is the past tense of 'shy', to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad plate carried on the arm to protect against blows is a form of armour.

clue.text: Spoof runner, backmarker in sprint

parts.note: a ski runs over snow, as a sledge's runner does

indicators.note: the backmarker of a race is at the rear, so the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A parody of an athlete who finishes last in a short race.
explanation.definitionFit: A short comic sketch sending something up is a send-up or parody.

clue.text: Suffering illness alongside career that's involved in graphic art

parts.note: suffering is pain
TB is tuberculosis
to career is to rush along at speed

explanation.surface: An ill artist suffers while making a living in illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's tool is used to make pictures, and painting is a graphic art.

clue.text: Prosecutor implicated in perverse network a man familiar with courts

indicators.note: implicated in means caught up inside, so the prosecutor goes in
perverse means turned the wrong way, so read backwards

parts.note: LAN is a local area network
DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A prosecutor caught up in a corrupt network knows his way around the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: The courts are tennis courts: Rafael Nadal is the Spanish tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish tennis great spent his career on tennis courts, so is at home there.

clue.text: Brand used by mum and kid

parts.note: Jo Brand is a British comedian
mum means silent, as in mum's the word, so sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: A product brand used by a mother and child.
explanation.walkthrough: Brand is the comedian Jo Brand, not a product; 'kid' is the verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease or rib them playfully.

clue.text: Inevitable accidents caused by cat and dog scuffling around settee mostly

indicators.note: the mixed animal letters go around the shortened seat
animals scuffling are tussling and jumbling about, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is used

parts.note: a settee is a sofa

explanation.surface: The pets fighting round the couch cause unavoidable mishaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the two pets splits into two words, with the shortened settee placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance language for natural disasters that no human could prevent or foresee.

clue.text: Theatrical show always attracts university backing

indicators.note: backing means the whole is read backwards
attracts means draws in, so the university letter goes inside

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A stage production always draws support from the university.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes into EVER to give EUVER; 'backing' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A light entertainment of sketches, songs and dances is a theatrical show.

clue.text: Spiritual film hides empty Sunday church

indicators.note: the film word hides, i.e. contains, the other pieces

parts.note: a pic is a picture, a film

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its insides, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A spiritual movie features an empty church on a Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the soul or to powers beyond the physical, as a medium claims.

clue.text: Such a haircut needs trimming regularly? Brickie goes first

indicators.note: goes first puts the bricklayer before the trimmed letters

parts.note: a bricklayer lays bricks, so is a layer

indicators.note: trimming the word regularly removes every other letter, keeping the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A tiered hairstyle needs frequent cutting; the bricklayer gets it done first.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut in which hair is shaped into tiers of different lengths is a familiar style.
